# Ownership and licence status

Six layers, never conflated:

| Layer | Who | Confers |
|---|---|---|
| machine nomination | machine | **nothing** |
| business assertion | BUSINESS_OWNER / BRAND_ADMIN | nothing — a belief |
| reviewed evidence | LEGAL/DESIGN reviewer | nothing — a fact on file |
| human confirmation | authorised human | settles a question |
| canonical activation | 2 humans, dual control | *which file is authoritative* |
| operational permissions | LEGAL / BRAND_ADMIN, per flag | *what the system may do* |

**Canonical activation grants no permission. Confirming ownership grants no
permission. Only an explicit, named, human permission grant does.**

## Independence of the axes

Technical readiness, ownership, licence, canonical status and operational permissions
are **five separate axes**. A technically perfect file with unconfirmed ownership is
unusable. A legally clean file that is the canonical master still has every permission
`false` until each one is granted by name.

## Real decisions on record

**Zero.** `0` events. No ownership has been confirmed, no
licence approved, no permission granted, no master activated — because no authorised
human has made those decisions yet. The machinery is ready; the decisions are theirs.
